tara: Anybody hit a weird interaction between coroutine cancellation + Retrofit + OkHttp dispatcher? In our Kotlin SDK sample the user backs out of the Activity, the suspend call gets cancelled but the underlying OkHttp Call sometimes lingers and fills the dispatcher. Then a token-refresh request gets queued behind it and we end up with delayed refresh + duplicate retries.

kevin: Which coroutine adapter are you using? retrofit2-kotlin-coroutines or a custom Call.await wrapper? Any repro snippets?

tara: We use a small internal suspend wrapper around Call.enqueue/Callback that resumes on response/failure. Repro steps: start a long streaming generate call (30s), then cancel the coroutine (navigate away). Meanwhile a 401 triggers token refresh from another short request. Because the long call didn't cancel quickly, OkHttp's Dispatcher (we tune it to maxRequests=8, maxRequestsPerHost=4) fills and the refresh request waits. When the refresh finally runs we occasionally get two refresh attempts (race) and the retry layer replays the original request -> duplicate side-effects. Logs: 

```
D/Retrofit: enqueue request /v1/generate
D/Coroutine: cancelled (Activity onPause)
W/OkHttp: call not canceled in time, queued
D/OkHttp: enqueue request /v1/auth/refresh (queued)
E/Auth: concurrent refresh triggered
D/OkHttp: request retried -> duplicate refresh
```

kevin: hmm. The common fix is to ensure the suspend wrapper cancels the Call when the coroutine is cancelled (invokeOnCancellation { call.cancel() }). Also consider using CallAdapter.Factory that integrates cancellation.

maria: plus add singleflight around token refresh so only one refresh happens even if multiple callers notice 401. That would stop dual refresh regardless of dispatcher queuing.

kevin: Another angle: tune Dispatcher so short auth calls can bypass long-running streaming ones (maxRequestsPerHost tweak), or mark streaming requests with a custom tag and use an Interceptor that deprioritizes them. But that's heavy. Simpler: make streaming calls non-retriable and coalesce refresh.

qa-bot: Created ticket DEVEX-8001: "Kotlin SDK: coroutine cancellation not canceling OkHttp Call causes queued token refreshes and duplicate retries" (<https://issues.redwood/DEVEX-8001>)

tara: I'll open a tiny repro app showing two coroutines (long + short) and the cancellation gap. PR will add: 1) utility suspend wrapper that cancels Call on coroutine cancel, 2) singleflight refresh mechanism, 3) docs note in onboarding about coroutine->Call cancellation.

maria: for telemetry, add EventListener tags so we can see counts of queued vs canceled calls and how often auth refresh was queued. That will help decide if we need dispatcher policies.

kevin: also test on emulator and Pixel 4/7 with network flakiness and verify we don't reintroduce duplicate refreshes. Add unit tests for the suspend wrapper and an integration test in sampleapp.

ci-bot: Linked DEVEX-8001 to SDK backlog and added labels: mobile, sdk, coroutines, high-priority.

tara: thanks all. will queue PR and paste repro apk in the ticket.
